status: GO-H1A rulings applied. Scope: README Layer A (option-dependent source-level branch-activation analysis). v3.1 = v3 after one wording refinement from the first bounded review (see amendments). Supersedes v3 (eligibility-rubric.v3-prereview.json), v2 and v1.
purpose: Assign each PR hunk an E category from source semantics only. Must not consult oba output, test presence, derivability (D), target validity (V), witnessability (W), or any historical verdict.

scope.in: Changes to an option's semantics (declaration, default, type, apply, readOnly, path) that are traceable to an option-dependent branch predicate; changes to a boolean predicate that directly or indirectly consumes option state.
out: Configuration-value assignments config.<path> = ... (U2): separate mode, not Layer A.
Changes to warning or assertion message text, or to data that a condition reads, when the condition expression itself is unchanged.
Shell or external-command tests (including inside derivation strings); their operands are command output, not Nix option state.
Test-only changes (witness only; counts for R, never for E).
Import-list registration, package-only changes, and runtime behavior or observability (README non-goals; layer C).

categories.E_DIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable to a branch predicate in the same module, OR a changed predicate whose changed term reads only options declared in the same module.
categories.E_INDIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable only to a predicate in another module, OR a changed predicate whose changed term reads an option declared in another module, OR whose option state reaches the changed term only through Nix-level let bindings or helper functions.
categories.E_AMBIGUOUS: Traceability or predicate status cannot be determined by the procedure below (search incomplete, truncated, unavailable, or an operand with no named option path). Not counted as E-positive; reported separately.
categories.E_NO: No change in scope: out-of-scope categories above, or traceability searched and absent, or an equivalent rewrite (EC10 with equivalence shown).

pr_aggregation: PR category = strongest hunk category in the order E_DIRECT > E_INDIRECT > E_AMBIGUOUS > E_NO. A hunk that declares several options takes the strongest option's category. E-positive = E_DIRECT or E_INDIRECT.

traceability_search.applies_to: Option-semantic changes (EC01-EC05, EC16-EC19). For a predicate change, the consumer check is used only to confirm that the changed predicate is in a branch construct; the category is set by predicate_rule.
traceability_search.unit: option path P of the changed option (for a removed option: base side; otherwise head side)
traceability_search.step1: Search the changed module file at the relevant side for a branch construct (mkIf, optional, optionals, if-then-else, assert, && or || or ! with a boolean operand, lib.mkMerge condition) whose operand reads P. A reference reads P if P appears in the changed expression or in an attribute path extending P (cfg.package.version reads cfg.package). Found in the same module file: T_IN.
traceability_search.step2: If not found in step1, search NixOS/nixpkgs at the same side for the option path or its last segment in nixos/modules with the branch-construct pattern. Found in another module: T_FOREIGN. Search executed with a complete result set and no branch consumer: T_NONE. Search truncated, rate-limited, unfiltered or unavailable: T_UNKNOWN.
traceability_search.record: For each traceability decision record: P, the search query or file searched, the predicate found (file, line, text) or the search result count, and T_*.

predicate_rule.changed_term: Only operands and operators the PR adds, removes or modifies count as the changed term. Unchanged operands are recorded as context.
predicate_rule.declaration_module_governs: The module that declares an operand decides the category of the changed term. A changed term that reads an option declared in another module is E_INDIRECT even when its consumer predicate is in the changed file. A changed term that reads only options declared in the changed module is E_DIRECT. Where the changed term mixes both, any foreign operand makes it E_INDIRECT.
predicate_rule.indirect_via_bindings: A changed term that reaches option state only through Nix-level let bindings or helper functions is E_INDIRECT. A let alias that is exactly an option path (cfg = config.x) is a direct read of x, not a binding.
predicate_rule.lambda_over_option_attrset: A predicate whose operand is a lambda parameter iterating an option attrset is traced to the iterated option path P, and P is then searched as in traceability_search. If the iterated attrset cannot be traced to a named option path, the result is T_UNKNOWN (E_AMBIGUOUS).
predicate_rule.not_nix_predicate: A predicate evaluated by a shell or by an external command (including inside a derivation string) is not an option-branch predicate: E_NO, even when its input path is derived from option values. Option state enters only as the iteration domain.
predicate_rule.data_only: A change to a value (list literal, package set, attribute value) that a predicate reads, when the predicate expression itself is unchanged and the option semantics are unchanged: E_NO (changes output or content only).

attribute_rule.rule: Helper-generated declarations (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating functions) are option declarations for protocol purposes; their arguments define default and type. Traceability applies to them as to hand-written declarations.

classes.name: removed option declaration
classes.rule: traceability_search on the removed path, base side

classes.name: default, type, or predicate expression rewritten
classes.rule: Show whether the evaluated value, accepted set, or branch outcome changes for every input. If not (for example a relocated or refactored predicate with equivalent evaluation): E_NO, with the equivalence stated. If yes: treat as EC03, EC04, or EC12. If not decidable from source: E_AMBIGUOUS.

classes.name: boolean predicate changed that consumes option state
warning or assertion condition changed
classes.rule: If the condition expression changed: predicate_rule. If only message text changed: E_NO. Only a Nix boolean condition is a predicate for this rule.

classes.name: rename or move of an option (mkRenamedOptionModule, mkRemovedOptionModule, explicit relocation)
classes.rule: traceability_search on the old path (base) and new path (head)

classes.name: option declared through a helper (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating function)
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05, with attribute_rule for helpers

classes.name: nested or submodule option
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05 at the nested path

classes.name: option declared with a dotted key
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05; key spelling is not a semantic change

classes.name: build-time check or derivation string test over option-derived values
classes.rule: not_nix_predicate: E_NO. A Nix-level boolean predicate in the same hunk is EC12.

classes.name: data change feeding a predicate, predicate expression unchanged, option semantics unchanged
import-list registration of a module file, or a test registration
classes.rule: E_NO by itself. The imported module's own declarations are classified under their own hunks.

amendments: v3.1 (after first bounded review): declaration_module_governs made explicit; the v3 result_map no longer sets the category of a predicate change (v3 contradicted predicate_rule for foreign operands in the same file).
v3.1: a reference extending an option path (cfg.package.version) reads that option; a changed expression that contains P reads P, including value arguments such as lib.optionals cond P.
v3.1: EC10 covers relocated or refactored predicates with equivalent evaluation (E_NO with equivalence stated).
v3.1: lambda_over_option_attrset rule added; predicates over lambda parameters with no traceable option path are E_AMBIGUOUS.
v3.1: aggregation over several options in one hunk; EC22 added for import-list and test registration lines.
known_gaps: Attribute attribution by text heuristics is unreliable for multi-line Nix strings; the adjudicator must read the parsed or indented structure.

Traceability across modules depends on search completeness. gh search code cannot filter by branch construct or pin a SHA; common option segments can exceed the result cap. Such cases are T_UNKNOWN and reported, never converted to E_NO.
Helper-generated declarations (EC17) may be invisible to text search; this affects D, not E.
